# John Skogman: ”Fått en zombiebörs”

**Feed**: efn-borsfrukost  
**Published**: 2026-08-25  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

EFN Morgon with trader John Skogman and analyst Martin Blomgren. Both see the Swedish economy as stronger than the gloomy mood suggests, but spending on bigger consumer goods is weak. Skogman calls the market a 'zombie market': constant outflows from small-cap funds and the shift to index funds have left companies outside the top 30 forgotten. He thinks this creates good buying opportunities, especially in net-cash companies on P/E 10-12, and the takeovers that follow. Company talk covered Ellos's Q2 report after its IPO, including an interview with its chair, outdoor retail (Amer Sports preferred over the struggling Swedish names), Nibe, Zinzino, Flat Capital, Klarna, Latour/Tomra, Skanska as a data-center winner, and trading in large caps such as Millicom and Klarna.

---

## Universe Stocks

### ⛔ ELLOS — Ellos | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Skogman: unnecessary IPO, below IPO price. Blomgren: no one will rush in, investors will wait. Lock-ups expire after year-end with bondholder owners.

#### Reasoning

Guest view (Skogman, backed by Blomgren): the company came quickly out of restructuring. Profit was wiped out by marketing and tax costs. Bondholder owners may sell when lock-ups expire after year-end. The small-cap market is weak and there are thousands of alternatives. Wait until the company has proven itself.

#### Sell Triggers

- if H2 results prove the turnaround
- if lock-up expiry passes without selling pressure
- if small caps re-rate broadly

> *"Så att man ska välja just Ellos i det här skedet i den konkurrensen, det finns ju en anledning till att man kan vänta"*

---

### 🟢 AS — Amer Sports | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Blomgren prefers the proven winner Amer over VF Corp despite the higher valuation, citing strong growth that looks set to continue.

#### Reasoning

Analyst Blomgren's view: Amer has built strong brands, sells accessories with good margins and has strong past growth that looks likely to continue. Paying the premium valuation for the proven winner is better than buying cheaper, struggling peers.

#### Sell Triggers

- if growth slows materially
- if valuation expands without earnings support

> *"landar jag ändå i att man nog ska gå på vinnaren som har bevisat sig även om de är lite dyrare värderingsmässigt"*

---

### ⛔ VFC — VF Corporation | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

More problems, similar to the struggling Fenix/RVRC. Lower valuation for a reason, including possible balance-sheet issues.

#### Reasoning

Blomgren favours Amer over VF. Skogman notes that big valuation gaps usually have an underlying cause and mentions possible balance-sheet problems at VF.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the turnaround in outdoor apparel shows up

> *"Medan WF Corp har lite mer problem."*

---

### ⛔ FOI-B — Fenix Outdoor | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Too many stores (Naturkompaniet, Germany), management seems tired, no turnaround work under way; stock down this year.

#### Reasoning

Skogman: Fenix has over-invested in physical stores, and its German stores are doing poorly. Management appears tired and is not driving change, unlike Björn Borg, which moved online successfully.

#### Sell Triggers

- if management change or a restructuring of the store network
- if German retail recovers

> *"Det går inte bra för dem och ledningen verkar rätt trött med det är inga förändringsarbeten där heller."*

---

### 🟡 NIBE-B — Nibe | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 50%

Strong German subsidy and sales data and a move into AC, but partly priced in and the stock isn't cheap, so not a rocket.

#### Reasoning

Skogman sees Nibe as a hedge for German energy fears and notes positive data. However, the German push has long been discussed and the valuation is full, so upside from the data is limited.

#### Sell Triggers

- if German heat-pump demand fades
- if energy prices normalise sharply

> *"Och Nibe är inte billigt heller, så säkert en liten uppgång idag, men Det kommer inte vara nån raket på de här siffrorna."*

---

### ⛔ ZZ-B — Zinzino | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Both guests dislike the MLM model ('pyramid-scheme feel') and pass despite the strong report reaction.

#### Reasoning

Skogman has always stayed away because of the multi-level-marketing business model and a volatile share price. Blomgren agrees and passes. This is a business-model objection, not about the numbers.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the business model changes away from MLM

> *"Fått lite pyramidspelkänsla av multilevel sales-bolag. Jag gillar inte Cincino."*

---

### ⛔ FLAT-B — Flat Capital | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Trades at a large premium to holdings, mostly Klarna. Not worth a premium unless it gets Klarna-Sebbe's dealflow.

#### Reasoning

Skogman: the case for owning Flat was access to Sebastian Siemiatkowski's dealflow. After selling other holdings it is mostly Klarna shares, so the premium to NAV is unjustified. Defensor is a bright spot, but Klarna must deliver.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Klarna shares re-rate strongly
- if Flat gains new attractive dealflow
- if premium to NAV closes

> *"Om du bara får Klarna-aktier när de har sålt mycket annat då är det inte värt att betala nån premie för Flat."*

---

### 🟢 KLAR — Klarna | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 50%

Sharp post-report fall on lowered growth; Skogman traded it and thinks it is at a fairly good level now.

#### Reasoning

Skogman sees the report as not that bad: the stock was punished for lowering its growth target even though profitability beat expectations. He sees a short-term trading opportunity after the overreaction.

#### Sell Triggers

- if growth guidance is cut further
- if Germany weakness spreads

> *"Och Klarna också. Jag tror att det är hyfsat bra läge där nu."*

---

### 🟢 TIGO — Millicom | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 45%

Skogman bought after last week's big fall and it bounced 7%.

#### Reasoning

Trader view: buying the dip after a sharp drop in a liquid large cap. Short-term trading, not a long-term thesis.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the bounce fades
- if the fall reflects fundamental deterioration

> *"Millicom hade ett jättestort fall här förra veckan. Då gick det att plocka upp lite aktier, det studsade upp 7 %."*

---

### ⛔ SAAB-B — Saab | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Skogman still thinks Saab is priced too high but is not currently short.

#### Reasoning

Skogman believes the defence stock is overvalued after the defence rally. He avoids shorting it because shorting frenzied stocks is dangerous.

#### Sell Triggers

- if valuation normalises
- if defence order growth accelerates further

> *"Jag tror ändå att Saab står för högt."*

---

### ⛔ LATO-B — Latour | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Premium turned into a discount. Weak holdings (Tomra, Sweco), underperforms peers. Skogman sceptical of CEO Hjertonsson's track record.

#### Reasoning

Skogman: Latour has underperformed other investment companies. Key holdings Tomra and Sweco have lagged, and he is not a fan of the CEO, whose past companies (Lammhult, Fagerhult) did not deliver.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Tomra and Sweco re-rate
- if the NAV discount widens to an attractive level

> *"Jag ser inte Latur som jätteköpbara, för aktiekursen har gått ner."*

---

### 🟠 SKA-B — Skanska | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Carnegie fund manager's top holding. Strong balance sheet, undervalued property management, possible extra dividends, data-center order tailwind.

#### Reasoning

Skogman cites Carnegie's Simon Blecher (manager opinion). A big cash pile, underappreciated property management, possible extra dividends and a construction recovery could give a double kick. Data-center orders add a structural tailwind. Risk: taking big contracts at thin margins.

#### Sell Triggers

- if it takes large contracts at underpriced margins
- if the data-center buildout stalls
- if the construction recovery fails

> *"Jag gillar tänket bakom, att Skanska har stor kassa."*

---

### 🟠 BABA — Alibaba | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Fell ~$30bn in value after a ~$10bn raise for AI; Skogman hints at a possible entry into Chinese consumers.

#### Reasoning

Speculative remark from Skogman: the dilution-driven drop looks outsized relative to the raise, which may offer exposure to the Chinese consumer.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI spending destroys value
- if Chinese consumer demand weakens

> *"Kanske ett läge på kinesiska konsumenter."*

---
